---
title: "Bubble plot — Eukaryotic classes across coral health states"
author: "Joana Krause"
date: "2026-01-05"
output: html_document
---

Bubble plot of mean relative abundance (± SD) of eukaryotic classes across all
coral health states (disease, healthy, bleached). Three concentric layers encode
variability: outer halo = mean + SD, middle ring = mean, inner core = mean − SD.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# Load libraries

```{r load-libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(rlang)   # sym() for tidy-eval rename
library(glue)    # glue() for dynamic plot title
```

# Load phyloseq object

```{r load-ps}
ps_plas_V3_V4 <- readRDS("../data/ps_final.rds")
```

# Sort taxa for axis ordering

`unique()` is used directly — the previous `toString() → strsplit(", ")` approach
silently breaks whenever a taxon name contains a comma.

```{r sort-taxa}
tax.sort <- as.data.frame(ps_plas_V3_V4@tax_table) %>%
  arrange(Domain, Supergroup, Division, Subdivision, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species)

order_sorted       <- c(unique(tax.sort$Order),       "Below Threshold")
family_sorted      <- c(unique(tax.sort$Family),      "Below Threshold")
class_sorted_auto  <- c(unique(tax.sort$Class),       "Below Threshold")
division_sorted    <- c(unique(tax.sort$Division),    "Below Threshold")
subdivision_sorted <- c(unique(tax.sort$Subdivision), "Below Threshold")  # FIX: was pulling Division
genus_sorted       <- c(unique(tax.sort$Genus),       "Below Threshold")
```


# Bubble plot — Relative Abundance of Eukaryotic Classes across coral health states

```{r bubble-plot}
## =============================================================================
## PURPOSE:
##   Visualises the mean relative abundance of eukaryotic classes (or any chosen
##   taxonomic rank) across sample groups as a bubble plot.
##   Three concentric layers encode variability:
##     - Outermost halo  → mean + SD  (faint, shows upper spread)
##     - Middle ring     → mean       (semi-transparent)
##     - Inner core      → mean − SD  (solid, shows lower spread)
##
## METHODOLOGY NOTE:
##   Each sample is normalised to 100 % independently BEFORE computing group
##   summaries. This gives true per-sample relative abundances, so the mean and
##   SD reflect biological variability rather than sequencing depth. Using
##   merge_samples() (which sums raw counts before normalising) is a known
##   phyloseq pitfall that biases both statistics and is intentionally avoided.
## =============================================================================

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 1) USER PARAMETERS
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ps_obj         <- ps_plas_V3_V4
group_var      <- "coral_health"
tax_rank       <- "Class"
mean_threshold <- 0.1       # taxa with overall mean < this % are collapsed
output_pdf     <- "../output/bub/bub_coralhealth_mean.pdf"

## X-axis group order
sample_order <- c("disease", "healthy", "bleached")

## Y-axis taxon order (bottom → top on the plot).
## Taxa absent from the data are silently ignored by ggplot.
class_sorted <- c(
  "Below Threshold",        # collapsed low-abundance taxa — always at the bottom
  "Eukaryota_XXXX",
  "Archaeplastida_XXX",
  # Chlorophyta_X
  "Ulvophyceae", "Trebouxiophyceae", "Prasino-Clade-9", "Pyramimonadophyceae",
  "Pedinophyceae", "Chloropicophyceae", "Chlorophyta_XX", "Chlorophyceae",
  "Chlorodendrophyceae",
  # Prasinodermophyta_X
  "Prasinodermophyceae", "Palmophyllophyceae",
  # Rhodophyta_X
  "Rhodophyta_XX", "Stylonematophyceae", "Florideophyceae",
  "Compsopogonophyceae", "Bangiophyceae",
  # Cryptophyta_X
  "Cryptophyceae",
  # Haptophyta_X
  "Prymnesiophyceae", "Pavlovophyceae",
  # Rhizaria - Cercozoa
  "Chlorarachniophyceae",
  # Alveolata - Apicomplexa
  "Coccidiomorphea",
  # Alveolata - Chrompodellids
  "Colpodellidea",
  # Alveolata - Dinoflagellata
  "Dinophyceae",
  # Stramenopiles - Gyrista
  "Pinguiophyceae", "Phaeophyceae", "Pelagophyceae", "Mediophyceae",
  "Gyrista_X", "Eustigmatophyceae", "Dictyochophyceae",
  "Diatomeae_X", "Coscinodiscophyceae", "Chrysophyceae", "Bacillariophyceae"
)

## Subdivision order for the fill legend
subdivision_order <- c(
  "Gyrista",
  "Chrompodellids", "Apicomplexa",
  "Haptophyta_X",
  "Cryptophyta_X",
  "Rhodophyta_X", "Prasinodermophyta_X", "Chlorophyta_X",
  "Archaeplastida_XX",
  "Eukaryota_XXX",
  "Other"
)

## Named colour palette — every level in subdivision_order must have an entry.
## Using a named vector means reordering subdivisions never misassigns colours.
palette <- c(
  "Gyrista"             = "#9C85C0",
  "Apicomplexa"         = "#E69F00",
  "Chrompodellids"      = "#4DAF4A",
  "Haptophyta_X"        = "#674C2A",
  "Cryptophyta_X"       = "#DDCC77",
  "Rhodophyta_X"        = "#BD0A36",
  "Prasinodermophyta_X" = "#377EB8",
  "Chlorophyta_X"       = "#ABC817",
  "Archaeplastida_XX"   = "purple4",
  "Eukaryota_XXX"       = "#00bfffff",
  "Other"               = "#999999"
)

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 2) Melt to long format (per-sample relative abundances)
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
##
##   tax_glom()                — merge ASVs sharing the same tax_rank label
##   transform_sample_counts() — normalise each sample to 100 % independently
##   psmelt()                  — reshape to long data frame
##   rename()                  — rename grouping column to "Group" for generality

melted <- ps_obj %>%
  tax_glom(taxrank = tax_rank) %>%
  transform_sample_counts(function(x) x / sum(x) * 100) %>%
  psmelt() %>%
  dplyr::rename(Group = !!sym(group_var))   # explicit namespace avoids base::rename conflict

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 3) Mean and SD per taxon × group
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
##
## Both statistics are computed in a single summarise() call on the same
## per-sample data, so they are guaranteed to correspond to each other.
## NA SD occurs when a group contains only one sample; replaced with 0
## (no spread can be computed, so the bubble shows no halo — correct behaviour).

dat1 <- melted %>%
  group_by(
    OTU, Group,
    across(all_of(tax_rank)),   # carry the taxonomic label column through
    Subdivision
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Abund_mean = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD         = sd(Abundance,   na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(SD = replace(SD, is.na(SD), 0))

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 4) Apply threshold, factor levels, SD bounds
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

dat1 <- dat1 %>%
  ## Overall mean per taxon (mean of per-group means, equally weighted).
  ## This is the value compared against mean_threshold.
  group_by(.data[[tax_rank]]) %>%
  mutate(mean_abund = mean(Abund_mean, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ## Collapse rare taxa: label replaced with "Below Threshold", subdivision
  ## set to "Other" so all rare taxa pool into one visual category.
  mutate(
    !!tax_rank  := if_else(mean_abund <= mean_threshold,
                           "Below Threshold", .data[[tax_rank]]),
    Subdivision  = if_else(mean_abund <= mean_threshold,
                           "Other", Subdivision)
  ) %>%
  ## Ordered factors control axis and legend order.
  mutate(
    Subdivision  = factor(Subdivision, levels = subdivision_order),
    tax_rank_fct = factor(.data[[tax_rank]], levels = class_sorted)
  ) %>%
  ## SD halo bounds, clamped above zero so scale_size_continuous never
  ## receives ≤ 0 input (which would make a bubble vanish or throw an error).
  mutate(
    Abund_upper = pmax(Abund_mean + SD, 1e-6),
    Abund_lower = pmax(Abund_mean - SD, 1e-6)
  )

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 5) Bubble plot
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
##
## Three geom_point layers, drawn largest-to-smallest so inner layers are
## always visible on top:
##   Layer 1 (α = 0.20): Abund_upper — faint outer glow (mean + SD)
##   Layer 2 (α = 0.60): Abund_mean  — semi-transparent ring (mean)
##   Layer 3 (α = 1.00): Abund_lower — solid core (mean − SD)
##
## When SD is small relative to the mean the three layers nearly overlap —
## this is correct behaviour, not a bug.

my_title <- glue("Eukaryotic {tax_rank} across coral health states — mean ≥ {mean_threshold}%")

bubp <- ggplot(
  dat1 %>% filter(Abund_mean > 0),   # suppress taxa absent from a given group
  aes(
    x = factor(Group, levels = sample_order),
    y = tax_rank_fct
  )
) +
  geom_point(   # outermost halo — mean + SD
    aes(size = Abund_upper, fill = Subdivision, color = Subdivision),
    alpha = 0.20, shape = 21, stroke = 0
  ) +
  geom_point(   # middle ring — mean
    aes(size = Abund_mean, fill = Subdivision, color = Subdivision),
    alpha = 0.60, shape = 21, stroke = 0
  ) +
  geom_point(   # inner solid core — mean − SD
    aes(size = Abund_lower, fill = Subdivision, color = Subdivision),
    alpha = 1.00, shape = 21, stroke = 0
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    limits = c(1e-6, 100),
    range  = c(0.1, 10),
    breaks = c(1, 10, 50, 75)
  ) +
  ## drop = TRUE: legend shows only subdivisions present in the data.
  ## Change to drop = FALSE if you need consistent legends across plot subsets.
  scale_fill_manual(values  = palette, drop = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = palette, drop = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x     = group_var,
    y     = tax_rank,
    size  = "Relative Abundance (%)",
    fill  = "Eukaryotic Subdivision",
    title = my_title
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  guides(
    color = "none",
    fill  = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))
  )

print(bubp)

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 6) Save to PDF
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

dir.create("../output/bub", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

pdf(output_pdf, width = 6, height = 6)
print(bubp)
dev.off()
```
